transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hello. Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to turn off my worrying. Once it starts, it just keeps going. Even when I tell myself I’ve made the lists, checked all the dates, and done everything I reasonably can to handle things, I still can't get my mind to stop fretting about it.
How long has this pattern of worrying been going on?

I'd say it's been going on for about seven months now. It started shortly after a friend of mine passed away. We had some projects we were doing together, and I tried to just... keep them moving along on my own after she died. That's really when all this started.
Are your worries mainly about your friend’s death and the projects you shared, or do they also occur about many other areas of your life?

It's really about a lot of other areas now. My mind just keeps roaming from one thing to another. I'll be thinking about the exhibition schedule, and then suddenly I'm worrying about my daughter's travel plans, or... or even just whether the house gutters need fixing. It just feels like these small, everyday things could suddenly unravel into something much bigger.
Before your friend died, did you have a similar pattern of worrying about many different areas of your life?

No, not really. I mean, I've always been an organized person—I like to plan things out and make sure everything is in order. But it never felt like this. Before she died, I could make a plan and then just... let it go. I didn't have this constant feeling that everything was going to fall apart if I stopped thinking about it.
Are the projects or other consequences related to your friend’s death still ongoing?
No, not anymore. I... I actually managed to finish up those projects a few months ago. So there isn't really anything from that still going on.
For how long after you finished those projects did the excessive worrying continue?

Well, the worrying started shortly after she died, when I was trying to keep all our projects moving. So, overall, this has been going on for about seven months now. Even after the projects were done, the worrying just... stayed.
Do you often feel restless or unable to sit still because of the worrying?

Yes, I do. I often feel... well, just wound up, even when I'm just sitting in my own living room. Like, if I'm on a phone call, I'll catch myself tapping my fingers the whole time. Or I'll just get up to straighten something out, mostly because sitting quietly just makes me feel jumpy.

{"intent":"Determine whether the anxiety has persisted for more than six months after the stressor and its consequences ended, which helps distinguish adjustment disorder from generalized anxiety disorder.","question":"Exactly how long ago did the projects end?""}
I'm not entirely sure of the exact date, to be honest. I just know it was a few months ago that everything finally wrapped up.
Did the projects end less than six months ago, or more than six months ago?

Less than six months ago, definitely. Since she only passed away about seven months ago, the projects finishing up would have been... well, maybe three or four months back? So yes, less than six months.
How has your sleep been since the excessive worrying began?
My sleep has been... well, it's been pretty normal, actually. I haven't really noticed any changes there. Even with everything going on, once I go to bed, I usually sleep just fine.
Have you been experiencing noticeable muscle tension since the worrying began?

Yes, I have. By the time evening rolls around, my shoulders and neck get so tight... I suppose it's from holding myself braced all day without really realizing it. I even catch myself clenching my jaw while I'm just sitting down to read, or when I'm trying to plan out the garden center activities.
Have you been feeling unusually tired during the day since this worrying began?

Yes, I have been. Even when I sleep through the night, I wake up feeling as if I have already put in half a day. By the time I just water the garden beds or sort some papers for my book club, I find that I need to sit down and just... gather myself. It's a very heavy kind of tired.
During the past six months, has this excessive worrying occurred on more days than not?

Yes, definitely on more days than not. Actually, it's been going on for about seven months now. It started shortly after my friend passed away... I was just trying to keep all of our projects moving along, and the worrying just seemed to start then and hasn't really stopped.
How much has this ongoing worry interfered with your daily activities, work, or relationships?

Well, I still manage to keep up with the garden center and my book club... but it's definitely having an impact. I've noticed I'm showing up less prepared than I usually would be. And... I've actually started turning down some of the responsibilities for the upcoming exhibition planning. It just feels harder to manage all those details than it used to. It's not stopping me completely, but it's making everything feel like much more of an effort.
If you set aside your friend’s death and the projects, do you still find yourself excessively worrying about unrelated areas of your life?

Yes, I do. It's not just about my friend or those projects. My mind just keeps roaming from one thing to another. I'll be thinking about the exhibition schedule, and then I'm suddenly worrying about my daughter's travel plans, or... or whether the house gutters need fixing. It just seems like even the small things start to feel as if they could unravel into something much bigger.
